title.narrative: Output 5.3. Increased capacity of the ILO constituents to design and deliver innovative, flexible and inclusive learning options, encompassing work-based learning and quality apprenticeships

description.narrative: The Government of Zanzibar through the President`s offices Labour, Economic Affair and Investment (PLEAI) and in collaboration with the Vocational Training Authority (VTA), in January 2020 developed and implemented skill development programmes targeting persons in vulnerable situations and youth not in education, employment or training (NEET). The programmes offered training in the occupations of carpentry, air conditions and refrigeration. The first batch of enrolments resulted in 100 young women and men being registered in the programme. The government has allocated approximately US$220,000 to support the expansion of the programme to 500 young women and men by 2021/22. With the support from Norway, the ILO provided technical support to the Government in the development and implementation of the skill development programmes in three vocational training centers.

description.narrative: The National Council for Technical Education (NECTA), in collaboration with Tanzania Commercial Bank (TCB), National Insurance Cooperation (NIC), and the Institute of Accountancy Arusha (IAA), in August 2021, developed and implemented quality undergraduate apprenticeship programmes in Bachelor Degree in Banking, Insurance and Risk Management, with apprenticeship. The first batches included 208 apprentices. Form July 2021, the ILO provided technical support on curriculum development and for the implementation of the training programmes.

description.narrative: The Prime Minister's Office Labour, Youth, Employment and Persons with Disability (PMO-LYED), Tanzania Mainland, and President`s offices Labour, Economic Affair and Investment (PLEAI) Zanzibar, conducted quality Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) assessment and certification in 2020. The programme covers ten occupations including welding and metal fabrication, electrical installation, auto body repair, motor vehicle mechanics, masonry and bricks laying, pipe fittings, carpentry and joinery, design, sewing and cloth technology, food production and food and beverage services. In December 2020, 12,000 candidates were assessed and certified in Tanzania Mainland and Zanzibar. Through the support from the Norway Foreign Ministry, ILO worked from March 2020, with the Prime Minister's Office Labour, Youth, Employment and Persons with Disability (PMO-LYED) and President`s offices Labour, Economic Affair and Investment (PLEAI), in collaboration with social partners; both in Mainland and Zanzibar in the designing and implementation of RPL assessments and certification using ILO tools
